title: Joshua Lim
text:
I’m a third year Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Statistical Science at Duke University, working with Jerry Reiter and Fan Li.
My research sits at the intersection of causal inference and missing data. Specifically, I seek to develop Bayesian methodology that can estimate heterogeneous treatment effects in the presence of missing data.
Before Duke I graduated summa cum laude from UCLA in 2024 with a B.S. in Applied Mathematics, Statistics and Data Science. Alongside my methods work I collaborate as a biostatistician with Duke, UC San Diego, and previously Stanford University Schools of Medicine — which keeps me honest about what messy, real clinical data actually looks like.
I am highly passionate about teaching. In Summer 2026 I was instructor of record for STA 199: Introduction to Data Science and Statistical Thinking.
Outside the department you’ll find me on the court with Duke Men’s Club Volleyball, performing with Duke Chinese Dance, flipping with Duke Gymnastics, or loudly defending UCLA sports deep in ACC country.

title: Teaching
text:
Earlier teaching

Math Speeder Upper Course — Introduction to Multivariable Calculus Summer 2021 Instructor and Curriculum Designer
A fully online introductory multivariable calculus course: 22 lectures, homework with solutions, quizzes, two midterms, three projects, and a final exam. Ten students in the first cohort, and new students still work through the now fully asynchronous material every year. Built to be accessible to any student regardless of background or socioeconomic status.


Physics Catcher Upper Course — Selected Topics from AP Physics Summer 2020 Instructor and Curriculum Designer
A fully online introductory physics course: 17 lectures, homework assignments and answer keys, a midterm, and a final exam.


Teaching Assistant, Menlo School Aug 2020 – Jun 2021 AP Statistics · AP Calculus BC · Advanced Topics in Probability and Statistics
Supported online, hybrid, and in-person formats. Wrote test questions, held help hours, led classroom activities, and ran problem-solving sessions with immediate feedback.


Private Tutor 2019 – present Mathematics, statistics, and physics
